name: Common WinUI converter and unit-normalization behavior

comparisons.reasoning: Two CairoBusinessDate converters identical including Arabic weekday table and dd/MM/yyyy. DateOnly input is already calendar date; DateTimeOffset uses dto.DateTime WITHOUT Cairo conversion, DateTime likewise unchanged, string parses current culture.
comparisons.callers_context: Converters.CallCenter201-214 versusCashier678-691 and immediate weekday arrays inspected; binding resource adapter, no server date calculation.
comparisons.financial_security_effects: No differing copy behavior; adapter name is stronger than timestamp semantics. A UTC instant near Cairo midnight can display source-offset date if bound directly, but normal business-date DateOnly binding unaffected; not independently confirmed UI defect.
comparisons.recommendation: Share one WinUI date converter with explicit DateOnly-versus-instant contract; preserve unknown emdash.

comparisons.reasoning: Two image converters cache absolute URI BitmapImage under static Dictionary lock, decode width320, return cached object, unsupported input null. Both caches are per-type/per-process, unbounded and no eviction shown.
comparisons.callers_context: CallCenter314-325/static fields309-312 versusCashier807-818/static fields800-805; ProductCatalogueView.xaml30 image binding verified.
comparisons.financial_security_effects: No auth-header injection or network authorization guarantee from BitmapImage here. Same body still separate assemblies/caches, not cross-client shared memory. Long-lived versioned URI churn can retain images; no measured leak/hardware claim.
comparisons.recommendation: Shared compatible WinUI image adapter and bounded cache/lifetime policy, preserve UI-thread affinity and URI version behavior.
tests: Bounded memory with changing menu images

comparisons.reasoning: TimeOfDay converters identical. DateTimeOffset ToLocalTime uses workstation zone then ar-EG formatting; DateTime formats supplied value without conversion.
comparisons.callers_context: CallCenter225-230 versusCashier702-707, adapter surface includes unsupported emdash.
comparisons.financial_security_effects: Display time can differ server Cairo policy on non-Cairo workstation, a shared assumption rather than copy divergence; no actual workstation timezone deployment test.
comparisons.recommendation: Share converter with explicit restaurant versus device-local time policy; preserve formatting contract.

comparisons.reasoning: OrderStatus labels normalize lower invariant then same Arabic names for pending/preparing/ready/completed/cancelled/refunded; unknown raw string retained, nonstring empty.
comparisons.callers_context: CallCenter13-22 versusCashier306-315; Cashier comment states lower-case wire DTO order status contract.
comparisons.financial_security_effects: No alternative financial status transition logic, label only; server state machine remains authoritative. Unknown names do not reject or authorize anything.
comparisons.recommendation: One shared status label map compatible with WinUI resources, do not alter server enum/state transitions.

comparisons.reasoning: Money display converters accept long/int, decimal divide100 and format2decimals with currency suffix. Null emdash; unexpected type silently0.00. Same Format helper bodies and contracts read.
comparisons.callers_context: CallCenter145-153 versusCashier622-630; menu/checkout/cash count bindings use Piastres fields.
comparisons.financial_security_effects: Display-only decimal prevents currency floating write; unsupported double/string can mask type mismatch as zero, not actual recorded zero money. No source divergence.
comparisons.recommendation: Share one typed money presentation adapter; consider explicit unknown on invalid type after UI contract tests, no change applied.

comparisons.reasoning: Visibility equality converters use ordinal comparison of value/parameter cast to string; both null becomes equal/Visible. Same type/parameter behavior on both clients.
comparisons.callers_context: CallCenter123-124/Cashier600-601; CallCenterOrderPanel175 payment method wallet binding verified.
comparisons.financial_security_effects: Presentation gating does not authorize payment; missing null parameter can show section, requiring binding contract tests. No financial actor enforcement here.
comparisons.recommendation: Share stateless visibility converter while preserving ordinal case and parameter semantics.

comparisons.reasoning: EmptyCollection visibility converter only recognizes nongeneric ICollection Count0 OR null, else collapsed. Identical copies.
comparisons.callers_context: CallCenter172-173 versusCashier649-650; collection-bound placeholder adapter, no row mutation.
comparisons.financial_security_effects: A lazy IEnumerable empty sequence without ICollection is treated nonempty/not-empty-state; ordinary ObservableCollection implements expected contract. No money calculation.
comparisons.recommendation: Shared converter or explicit collection-count binding, preserve distinction null and unsupported collection types.

comparisons.reasoning: CountGreaterThanOne converter recognizes ICollection Count>1 only. Null/unsupported/one/zero collapsed, copies identical.
comparisons.callers_context: CallCenter133-134 versusCashier610-611; ProductCatalogue variant chooser visibility binding47 verified.
comparisons.financial_security_effects: Only presentation of variant control, not server item selection validation. No authorization or variant price formula duplicated.
comparisons.recommendation: Share converter with stateless collection contract; keep threshold>1 distinct other collection adapters.

comparisons.reasoning: NonEmpty converter recognizes ICollection Count>0 only, not arbitrary IEnumerable. Both identical, different predicate intentionally from Empty and GreaterThanOne.
comparisons.callers_context: CallCenter183-184 versusCashier660-661; same WinUI IValueConverter adapters.
comparisons.financial_security_effects: No financial data collection or side effects; do not merge distinct thresholds into one implicit rule.
comparisons.recommendation: Share parameterized converter only with explicit threshold/null policy and compatible resource facades.

comparisons.reasoning: Four Arabic-digit normalization lambdas identical: ArabicIndic/EasternIndic digits to ASCII, Arabic decimal mark to dot. Parent parsers differ: CashInput decimal2digits/nonnegative/maxlong100; MilliUnits decimal3digits/maxlong1000; Attendance finite double hours/nonnegative or nonnegative int count.
comparisons.callers_context: Exact lambdas read in both CashInput, MilliUnits18-22 and Attendance146-153; prior full CashInput clone comparison preserved.
comparisons.financial_security_effects: Only character transformation reusable. Sharing whole parser would wrongly impose currency precision on inventory/hours. Financial source server validation independent; client parser alone does not fix signed raw API bounds.
comparisons.recommendation: Extract pure normalization helper if compatible, retain distinct unit-specific precision/range/parsing rules.
